checklist: Play S1 from the perimeter wall through the first fighter pair in all three rigs; confirm the classic ship silhouette shows through near structures and nowhere else.
Shoot parked fighters, FUEL drums, radar and turrets; confirm decor (grey tarped fighters, horizontal tanks, roof flak) never reads as a target.
Thread wall gaps, electric barriers and debris gates; check THREAD/PERFECT THREAD/LOW PASS and graze awards and that the altimeter band matches each opening.
Finish a sector with no damage both below and above 35% targets; the clean bonus must only pay above.
Watch the grade card land over the closing fuel lane and yield to the next sector card; check the results grade chips and BEST GRADES after two runs.
Copy the results FORTRESS CODE, open the game with ?seed=CODE and confirm the same fortress; fly DAILY SORTIE twice on one day.
Boss: pods, core, then the rack duel from phase two (lean-in, lock on rack, RACK n/6); listen for the curtain sweep dropping out at the gap.
Listen through a whole run on speakers and headphones: sector hooks in S1, S4, S7 and the boss, ambient beds per environment, and ducking under big blasts.
Continue into loop 2 and check score banking and harder pacing.
Test controller, touch, portrait and landscape; use F for telemetry on named hardware during crowded combat and the boss.

open_items: Human playtest of the full campaign: opening pace, sector grades, clean-bonus threshold (35%), debris gates, electric barriers and the rack duel.
Audio audition by ear: hooks, environment beds, the curtain-gap sweep, limiter behaviour in dense combat, and stereo placement.
Physical controller and touch acceptance, portrait and landscape HUD in real devices.
Named-hardware sustained FPS, p95 frame pacing and repeated-restart GPU memory.

Round-2 critic items not taken: one lane-shape rule per fortress sector (the playable lane is still one template), wall-mounted guns (they would sit outside the firing lane and break level forward gunfire), and staging the boss curtain from the arena pylons with a core-chamber wall.
Exposure: reactor (ember) classic frames still measure about 21 luma and space classic about 18; raising them further needs a deck-tint or key-light change, not bloom.
The S1 opening keeps the gentle 900-unit authored pace at the user's earlier request; the critic suggested trimming it to about 450.

project_constraints: Polish the existing eight-sector campaign; preserve the three accepted camera rigs.
Keep classic orthographic flight, level forward gunfire and altitude-dependent targeting; steering shots requires Flight Assist.
Keep local procedural assets, seeded level data, synthesized audio and pooled effects.
Approaching hazards remain opaque; retire cleared obstacle visuals and cut away foreground decoration.
Keep source-review scores separate from rendered tests and human acceptance.
Juice comes from geometry, vertex animation and authored emissive detail inside existing batches, not from more bloom, post-processing or lights.
Keep the composer target samples: 0 and emissive gains authored around the 1.02 bloom threshold.
Keep the light count constant (lights sit at zero intensity when idle); changing it recompiles every lit material.

architecture.entry: src/main.js owns boot, menu actions and coordinated shutdown
architecture.engine: src/core/Engine.js owns renderer, one RAF, adaptive resolution, input and bounded substeps
architecture.simulation: src/game/Game.js owns state, spawning, swept collision, scoring and campaign progression
architecture.presentation: Game.lateUpdate runs camera, effects, projectile uploads and DOM HUD once per rendered frame
architecture.world: Level produces seeded data (sector phrases, perimeter walls, debris gates, carrier launches); Fortress stamps chunks from cached templates into pooled per-material buffers with baked AO and approach/side tint lifts, building the chunk under the ship first and further chunks only inside a 6 ms measured build slice.
architecture.visibility: CombatVisibility projects target centers with a 4 percent screen-edge margin. AltitudeEcho chooses one forward-lane target; sightlines honor solid cover using parallel orthographic or perspective rays, and the candidate firing path is traced against collision geometry.
architecture.render: RenderPass, HDR-threshold bloom, ACES/sRGB output and one composite pass. Emissive strips animate in the shared neon vertex shader (LIGHT_ANIM); dishes, fans and wreckage spin in the vertex shader (Materials.addSpin). Underlay plane and flight grid owned by Engine.
architecture.audio: Web Audio synthesis: SONGS table with A/B phrases and hooks, lookahead scheduler, sfx and music buses, duck plus low-shelf and cue-band pocket, glue compressor, brick-wall compressor, unity-gain tanh clipper, per-room convolver, environment beds; offline rendering via init(offlineCtx) and at(seconds).
architecture.prewarm: Game.prewarm stages one chunk per sector, every enemy, the boss, pickups, instanced effects, both force fields and the classic silhouette, then main.js compiles against the composer target and uploads every staged texture. Shared materials that own unique programs (pickup halos, boss core, force fields) are never disposed mid-run, so the program count stays flat.

resource_ownership.application: Lifetime owns event subscriptions and cancellable waits; shutdown disposes actors before shared caches.
resource_ownership.shared: Materials and Textures own reusable materials/textures; enemy and pickup caches live until application shutdown.
resource_ownership.instances: Fortress owns streamed geometry; actors own private geometry and flash/core materials; pools own their instance buffers.
resource_ownership.visibility_queries: Reusable scalar/vector/box scratch storage; sightline queries do not mutate gate collision caches or retain actor references.
resource_ownership.altimeter: HUD owns one fixed DOM contact band and reusable snapshot; no per-enemy DOM nodes or actor references. Combo and sector text animations are canceled when replaced and on reset/disposal.

known_tradeoffs: Procedural texture anisotropy still changes only after reload; other quality budgets switch live.
Partial constructor failures can leave allocations outside the outer shutdown owner.
Simulation uses up to four bounded variable substeps, not a fixed-step accumulator.
Projectile tests use moving enemy current centers; moving gates have previous/current face sweeps.
Viewport eligibility is based on the target center or boss impact point, not GPU occlusion queries. Physical cover blocks bullets; altimeter sightlines separately respect approaching walls/gates.
No new independent critic scores were assigned during this maintenance pass.
Altimeter contact describes the next muzzle lane and current target position; moving targets still require player timing.
Slower travel preserves baseline fuel per distance, but longer exposure to enemy fire and sector encounter weights still need human campaign balancing.
Pickup halos share one material per colour, so they pulse in size rather than opacity.
The space and arena reverb tails are generated 1.5 s after audio start; a space sector entered sooner would keep the fortress room until they exist.
Decorative fighters, drums and flak are deliberately grey and inert; only orange-livery objects are targets.
The boss core material is shared across loops and owned by Materials rather than the Boss instance.

performance_targets.memory: Require a stable post-warm-up geometry/texture/GPU-memory plateau across ten retries, quality switching and a complete campaign.
performance_targets.measurement_limits: Current render-call/triangle counts are controlled 1280x720 scene snapshots, not sustained FPS or GPU byte measurements.
